**Draft notes**

Tells found: bold labels on each paragraph (§19), an en dash in the title and the pay range (§8), a forced triad in "real days off, nights that actually end, and a schedule you can plan a life around" (§6), and "real" used twice for emphasis. The rest is already specific and reads like a person wrote it, so I left it alone.

**Remaining patterns:** The first paragraph has a three-part "run the line / keep the crew steady / still care about the salt" sequence. I kept it because each part is a distinct duty and the last one carries the voice.

<final>
Sous chef, Brasa Norte (Portland, OR)

We cook over fire, we're slammed on the weekends, and we like it that way. Brasa Norte is looking for a sous chef who can run the line when the chef isn't there, keep the crew steady when tickets stack up, and still care about whether the salt is right on the third plate of the night.

We're open Wednesday through Sunday, dinner only. That means real days off and nights that actually end, so you can plan a life around the schedule. The job is full time and hands-on: you'll be on the line most nights and running the kitchen when it counts.

You'll lead service, run prep, order and receive, and train and coach cooks, keeping standards high without turning the kitchen into a pressure cooker. You'll work closely with the chef on menu changes and specials, and you'll have a say in how we do things.

We're after someone who's done this before, ideally with live fire or grill experience, and who's ready for the next step up. You're organized, calm when it gets loud, and the kind of person cooks want to work for.

Pay is $68,000 to $75,000 a year, depending on experience.

If that sounds like your kind of kitchen, send us a note and tell us where you've cooked and what you're proud of.
</final>
